Abdominal wall anatomy: 3

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

An anatomical section shows a paired vertical muscle near the anterior midline, enclosed by an aponeurotic sheath. Which abdominal muscle best matches this location rather than the lateral oblique or transverse layers?

  1. Inguinal ligament
  2. Rectus abdominis
  3. Camper fascia
  4. Scarpa fascia
  5. Transversalis fascia
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Rectus abdominis

Rectus abdominis is a paired vertical anterior abdominal muscle enclosed by the rectus sheath.

Understanding the options

Rectus abdominis
Rectus abdominis is a paired vertical anterior abdominal muscle enclosed by the rectus sheath.
Camper fascia
Camper fascia is the fatty superficial layer of abdominal subcutaneous tissue. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Scarpa fascia
Scarpa fascia is the deeper membranous layer of lower anterior abdominal subcutaneous tissue. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Transversalis fascia
The transversalis fascia lies deep to the transversus abdominis and contributes to the deep inguinal ring. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Inguinal ligament
The inguinal ligament is formed by the rolled inferior border of the external oblique aponeurosis. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
